blocks.text: Yeh chapter 30 (Spectroscopy-2 NMR) ke poore chapter se practice long questions (tafseeli sawal) hain, Board ke long question ki shakal mein: har sawal 4 number ka hai (wazahat, equations, zaroorat ho to diagram), aur chapter ke numericals qadam ba qadam hal kiye gaye hain. Har sawal ka poora model jawab hai.

blocks.prompt:
1 What is NMR spectroscopy? Give its uses and name its two common methods. Explain why only some nuclei give NMR signals. (4 marks)
(NMR spectroscopy kya hai? Is ke istemal aur do aam methods likhein. Wazahat karein ke sirf kuch nuclei NMR signal kyun dete hain.)
blocks.explanation:
Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy aik taqatwar technique hai jo nuclei ki magnetic properties (nuclear spin) par mabni hai.

Istemal: chemistry, polymer industry, proteins aur natural products ka mutaala, environment monitoring aur medical field. Chemistry mein khaas taur par organic compounds ki pehchaan aur un ki structure maloom karne ke liye.

Do aam methods: proton (¹H) NMR aur carbon-13 (¹³C) NMR.

Kaun se nuclei signal dete hain: odd mass number wale atoms, maslan ¹H aur ¹³C, aam taur par signal dete hain; un ke nuclei chhote magnets ki tarah hote hain. Even atomic aur even mass number wale nuclei, maslan ¹²C, mein protons aur neutrons even hote hain (hamesha barabar nahi; ¹⁸O mein 8 protons aur 10 neutrons). Protons apne spins jorr lete hain aur neutrons apne, is liye khalis magnetic field nahi aur NMR signal nahi.

book_ref.quote: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is a powerful technique

blocks.prompt:
2 Describe the principle of proton (¹H) NMR spectroscopy. Use methanol to explain how NMR identifies hydrogen atoms in different environments. (4 marks)
(Proton (¹H) NMR spectroscopy ka usool bayan karein. Methanol ki misaal se samjhayein ke NMR mukhtalif environments ke hydrogen atoms kaise pehchanti hai.)
blocks.explanation:
Nuclear spin: ¹H jaise nuclei chhote magnets ki tarah hote hain.

1. Magnetic field nahi: tamam nuclei be-tarteeb rukh mein aur aik jaisi energy ke.
2. Taqatwar magnetic field: nuclei field ke saath ya khilaf align hote hain, do spin states bante hain, low energy aur high energy (Figure 30.1).
3. Spin flipping: radio waves dalne par low energy state ke nuclei energy jazb kar ke high energy state mein chale jate hain.
4. Spectrum: asal state mein wapas aate waqt woh energy kharij karte hain jo detect ho kar NMR spectrum banti hai.

Molecular environment: nucleus ko flip karne ki exact energy compound mein us ki jagah aur ird gird ke atoms (molecular environment) par munhasir hai. Is liye aik molecule ke mukhtalif environments ke hydrogens mukhtalif energy jazb karte hain.

Methanol, CH₃OH: teen hydrogens carbon par aur aik oxygen par. -CH₃ aur O-H hydrogens mukhtalif environments mein hain, is liye flip hone ke liye mukhtalif frequencies jazb karte hain aur alag signals dete hain.

Agar magnetic field ki taqat badli jaye to mukhtalif environments ke nuclei aik hi frequency ki radio waves se bhi flip ho sakte hain.

book_ref.quote: When placed in a strong magnetic field, these nuclei align themselves

blocks.prompt:
3 Explain the problem caused by ordinary solvents in ¹H NMR and how deuterated solvents solve it. Why is TMS added as well? (4 marks)
(¹H NMR mein aam solvents se paida hone wala masla aur deuterated solvents us ka hal kaise karte hain, wazahat karein. TMS bhi kyun daala jata hai?)
blocks.explanation:
Masla: sample zyada solvent mein hal kiya jata hai. Aam solvents ke hydrogen atoms taqatwar signals de kar spectrum mein mudakhlat karte hain. Agar CHCl₃ istemal ho to us ke aik proton ka signal itna taqatwar hota ke sample ke protons ke kamzor signals ko poori tarah chhupa deta.

Hal: CDCl₃ (deuterated chloroform) ya CD₃OD (deuterated methanol) jaise deuterated solvents istemal hote hain. CDCl₃ mein hydrogen ki jagah us ka isotope deuterium (D) hai. Deuterium ko flip hone ke liye mukhtalif radio frequency chahiye, is liye woh sample wali frequency jazb nahi karta aur ¹H spectrum mein peak nahi deta. Solvent 'silent' hai aur sirf sample ke signals nazar aate hain.

TMS: tetramethylsilane, Si(CH₃)₄, standard reference hai. Is ka signal 0.0 ppm rakha jata hai aur baqi har signal isi se napa jata hai. Is ke 12 equivalent protons bilkul daayen (silicon ki kam electronegativity) aik sharp peak dete hain, aksar organic signals se door; yeh inert aur volatile hai, is liye aasani se nikal jata hai.

book_ref.quote: In the ¹H NMR analysis the sample to be analyzed is dissolved in excess solvent

blocks.prompt:
4 Define chemical shift. Explain how the electron density around a proton affects its chemical shift, using the spectrum of methanol. (4 marks)
(Chemical shift ki definition likhein. Methanol ke spectrum ki misaal se samjhayein ke proton ke ird gird electron density us ke chemical shift par kya asar dalti hai.)
blocks.explanation:
Chemical shift (δ): ¹H NMR spectrum mein TMS peak ke muqable mein kisi peak ki jagah; yeh parts per million (ppm) mein napa jata hai. TMS ko 0.0 ppm diya jata hai. ¹H spectrum ki δ range 0 – 12 ppm hai.

Chemical shift proton ka electronic environment batata hai: mukhtalif environments ke protons ke δ mukhtalif, aik environment walon ke δ aik jaise.

Electron density ka asar: protons electrons se ghire hote hain aur yeh electron density spectrum par asar dalti hai.
• Zyada electron density (alkyl groups) wale protons ka δ kam hota hai.
• Kam electron density wale protons, jo F, O, N, Cl jaise electronegative atoms ke qareeb hon, zyada δ par aate hain.

Methanol (Figure 30.2): -CH₃ protons ke ird gird electron density zyada hai aur woh 3.35 ppm par aate hain. O-H proton electronegative oxygen ke saath hai aur 4.80 ppm par aata hai. Har peak ka TMS peak (0.0 ppm) se faasla us ka chemical shift hai.

book_ref.quote: Chemical shift is an important parameter in NMR spectroscopy

blocks.prompt:
5 What are chemically equivalent protons? Explain with examples of molecules having one, two and three proton environments. (4 marks)
(Chemically equivalent protons kya hain? Aik, do aur teen proton environments wale molecules ki misaalon se samjhayein.)
blocks.explanation:
Molecule ke mukhtalif hisson ke protons qareeb ke atoms aur bonds ki wajah se mukhtalif environments mein hote hain.

Chemically equivalent protons: molecule mein aik jaise chemical environment wale tamam protons. Un ka chemical shift aik hota hai.

Aik environment: TMS, methane, ethane, benzene aur propanone (acetone) ke tamam protons equivalent hain, is liye har aik aik absorption peak deta hai (Figure 30.3, methane).

Do environments: methanol, CH₃OH. Teen -CH₃ protons aik set aur O-H proton doosra; do peaks (3.35 aur 4.80 ppm).

Teen environments: ethanol, C₂H₅OH. -CH₃ ka proton -CH₂- aur O-H ke protons se mukhtalif hai. Teen -CH₃ protons ka aik environment aur do -CH₂- protons ka doosra, is liye teen sets aur teen peaks.

Jis molecule mein mukhtalif protons ke sets hon us ke chemical shifts mukhtalif hote hain aur woh aik se zyada peaks deta hai.

book_ref.quote: Protons in different parts of a molecule are in different "environments"

blocks.prompt:
6 What information does a low-resolution ¹H NMR spectrum give? Interpret the low-resolution spectrum of ethanol (Figure 30.4). (4 marks)
(Low-resolution ¹H NMR spectrum kya maloomaat deta hai? Ethanol ke low-resolution spectrum (Figure 30.4) ki tashreeh karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Low-resolution spectrum teen bunyadi maloomaat deta hai: protons ke mukhtalif environments ki tadaad, un ki qisam aur har aik mein protons ki nisbati tadaad. Teen parameters dekhe jate hain:

1. Peaks ki tadaad: protons ke mukhtalif chemical environments ki tadaad.
2. Har peak ka chemical shift: environment ki qisam (Table 30.1 se muqabla).
3. Har peak ke neeche area: us peak wale protons ki tadaad ke mutanasib.

Ethanol, CH₃CH₂OH (Figure 30.4):
• Teen peaks, yani teen proton environments: CH₃, CH₂ aur OH.
• 5.4 ppm: OH (kam electron density); 3.7 ppm: oxygen ke saath –CH₂–; 1.2 ppm: –CH₃.
• Peaks par 1H, 2H aur 3H: areas 1 : 2 : 3, jo OH (1), CH₂ (2) aur CH₃ (3) se milte hain.
• Kul hydrogens = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6.

book_ref.quote: A low-resolution ¹H NMR spectrum provides three main pieces of information

blocks.prompt:
7 A compound C₈H₁₀ gives three ¹H NMR peaks at 7.2, 2.6 and 1.2 ppm with relative areas 16.0 : 6.4 : 9.6. Find the number of protons in each environment and identify each type of proton using Table 30.1. (4 marks)
(Compound C₈H₁₀ 7.2, 2.6 aur 1.2 ppm par teen ¹H NMR peaks deta hai jin ke nisbati areas 16.0 : 6.4 : 9.6 hain. Har environment ke protons maloom karein aur Table 30.1 se har qisam ke proton ki pehchaan karein.)
blocks.explanation: Peak area protons ki tadaad ke mutanasib hai: areas ko poore adadon ki nisbat mein layein, formula se check karein, phir δ ranges se qisam pehchanein.

book_ref.quote: The intensity ratio shows that they are present in the ratio of 1:2:3

steps: Poore adad ke liye 2 se zarb: 5 : 2 : 3
Majmooa = 5 + 2 + 3 = 10, jo C₈H₁₀ ke 10 H ke barabar hai, is liye peaks 5 H, 2 H aur 3 H ki hain
7.2 ppm (5 H): 6.5 – 9.0 ppm mein, aromatic protons Ar–H
2.6 ppm (2 H): 2.3 – 3.0 ppm mein, aromatic ring ke saath –CH₂–
1.2 ppm (3 H): 0.5 – 1.5 ppm mein, alkyl –CH₃
blocks.final_answer: 5 H (Ar–H, 7.2 ppm), 2 H (–CH₂–Ar, 2.6 ppm) aur 3 H (–CH₃, 1.2 ppm): compound C₆H₅–CH₂–CH₃ (ethylbenzene) hai.

blocks.prompt:
8 What is meant by splitting of signals in high-resolution ¹H NMR? State the n+1 rule and explain the high-resolution spectrum of ethanol. (4 marks)
(High-resolution ¹H NMR mein signals ki splitting se kya muraad hai? n+1 rule bayan karein aur ethanol ka high-resolution spectrum samjhayein.)
blocks.explanation:
NMR signals sirf qareeb ke electrons se nahi balke saath wale atoms ke protons se bhi mutasir hote hain. High-resolution spectrum mein har peak aksar sub-peaks ka guchha hoti hai, kyun ke har signal saath wale carbon atoms ke protons se split hota hai.

Signals ki splitting: multiple peaks (doublets, triplets, quartets) mein splitting saath wale carbon atom par protons ki tadaad batati hai.

n+1 rule: signal aam taur par n + 1 sub-peaks mein split hota hai, jahan n saath wale carbon atom(s) par protons ki tadaad hai.
Sub-peaks ki tadaad = n + 1

Ethanol, CH₃–CH₂–OH (Figure 30.5):
• -CH₃: saath wale carbon par 2 protons, 2 + 1 = 3 sub-peaks: triplet.
• -CH₂-: saath wale carbon par 3 protons, 3 + 1 = 4 sub-peaks: quartet.
• -OH: split nahi hota kyun ke us ka hydrogen carbon ki bajaye oxygen se jura hai: singlet.

book_ref.quote: When a high-resolution ¹H NMR spectrum of a molecule is studied

blocks.prompt:
9 Which protons do not show or cause splitting? Explain with ethane. Give the common splitting patterns of Table 30.2. (4 marks)
(Kaun se protons splitting nahi dikhate ya nahi karte? Ethane ki misaal se samjhayein. Table 30.2 ke aam splitting patterns likhein.)
blocks.explanation:
Splitting na hone ki soorat:
1. -OH aur -NH protons aam taur par split nahi hote; singlet ki shakal mein aate hain.
2. Chemically equivalent protons apne parosi protons ko split nahi karte.

Ethane, CH₃–CH₃: aik methyl group ko dekhein to saath wale carbon par 3 protons hain, is liye quartet ki tawaqqo hoti. Magar ethane ke chhe hydrogens chemically equivalent hain, is liye peak split nahi hoti; ethane aik singlet deta hai (Figure 30.6).

Aam splitting patterns (Table 30.2):

book_ref.quote: Similarly, chemically equivalent protons do not cause splitting of their neighbouring protons

blocks.prompt:
10 Use the n+1 rule to find the number of sub-peaks and the splitting pattern of every signal of methyl propanoate, CH₃–CH₂–CO–O–CH₃. (4 marks)
(n+1 rule se methyl propanoate, CH₃–CH₂–CO–O–CH₃, ke har signal ke sub-peaks aur splitting pattern maloom karein.)
blocks.explanation: Har equivalent protons ke set ke liye n ginein, yani saath wale carbon atom(s) par protons; phir sub-peaks = n + 1. Baghair hydrogen wale atoms (C=O carbon, O) n mein kuch nahi jorte.

book_ref.quote: Number of sub-peaks can be calculated by using 'n+1' rule

steps: Environments: CH₃ (ethyl hissa), CH₂ (C=O ke saath) aur O–CH₃: teen signals
Ethyl hisse ka CH₃: saath wale CH₂ par 2 H, n = 2, sub-peaks = 2 + 1 = 3: triplet
CH₂: saath wale CH₃ par 3 H aur C=O carbon par koi nahi, n = 3, sub-peaks = 3 + 1 = 4: quartet
O–CH₃: parosi O hai (H nahi), n = 0, sub-peaks = 0 + 1 = 1: singlet
Integration: 3 : 2 : 3 (kul 8 H, C₄H₈O₂)
blocks.final_answer: CH₃ triplet (3 sub-peaks), CH₂ quartet (4 sub-peaks), O–CH₃ singlet (1 sub-peak); areas 3 : 2 : 3.

blocks.prompt:
11 A compound shows two singlets and it is not clear which is due to an O-H proton. Explain why such a proton is hard to identify, and how deuterium exchange settles it. Give the equations. (4 marks)
(Aik compound do singlets deta hai aur wazeh nahi ke O-H proton kaun sa hai. Wazahat karein ke aisa proton pehchanna mushkil kyun hai aur deuterium exchange se faisla kaise hota hai. Equations likhein.)
blocks.explanation:
Mushkil kyun: O-H (alcohols, carboxylic acids) aur N-H (amines, amides) ke hydrogens aasani se badal jate hain, is liye un ke singlet ka δ wasee range mein hota hai aur pehchanna mushkil hai. Ethanol ka paani se exchange:
CH₃–CH₂–O–Hᵃ + Hᵇ–O–Hᵇ ⇌ CH₃–CH₂–O–Hᵇ + Hᵃ–O–Hᵇ

Deuterium exchange (D₂O shake):
1. ¹H spectrum lein; yeh O–H samet tamam H atoms dikhata hai.
2. Sample tube mein D₂O ke chand qatre daal kar achhi tarah hilayein aur spectrum dobara lein.
3. Muqabla: jo singlet doosre spectrum mein ghayab ho gaya woh O–H proton ka tha; jo reh gaya woh C–H protons ka hai.

Wajah: O ya N jaise zyada electronegative atoms se jure protons jaldi deuterium se badal jate hain:
R–O–H + D₂O ⇌ R–O–D + HOD
Deuterium ko spin flip ke liye ¹H se mukhtalif energy chahiye, is liye ¹H spectrum mein peak nahi deta; 'invisible' hai.

book_ref.quote: Sometimes, it becomes very difficult to identify these peaks in spectra

blocks.prompt:
12 Describe the steps for predicting the ¹H NMR spectrum of a molecule. Apply them to ethanal, CH₃CHO. (4 marks)
(Kisi molecule ka ¹H NMR spectrum predict karne ke qadam bayan karein. Inhein ethanal, CH₃CHO, par lagayein.)
blocks.explanation:
Qadam:
I. Protons ke mukhtalif environments pehchanein; environments ki tadaad = mutawaqqa peaks.
II. Table 30.1 se har set ka δ andaza lagayein; table na ho to qareeb ke bonds aur atoms dekhein (electronegative elements ke qareeb: zyada δ; alkyl: kam δ).
III. n+1 rule se har peak ki splitting predict karein.
IV. Har environment ke H atoms ke mutabiq integration ratios dein.

Ethanal, CH₃–CHO:

book_ref.quote: After understanding the concepts of chemical environment, chemical shift and splitting of peaks

blocks.prompt:
13 Predict the ¹H NMR spectrum of bromoethane, CH₃–CH₂–Br, and of methoxymethane, CH₃–O–CH₃. Explain why the two spectra differ. (4 marks)
(Bromoethane, CH₃–CH₂–Br, aur methoxymethane, CH₃–O–CH₃, ke ¹H NMR spectra predict karein. Wazahat karein ke dono spectra mukhtalif kyun hain.)
blocks.explanation:
Bromoethane, CH₃–CH₂–Br (Example 30.1 ki tarah):
• Peaks: do environments (CH₃ aur CH₂), is liye 2 peaks.
• δ: CH₂ electronegative halogen se jura hai, is liye zyada δ (3.0 – 4.5 ppm); CH₃ kam (0.5 – 1.5 ppm).
• Splitting: CH₃ ke 2 parosi H, 2 + 1 = 3: triplet; CH₂ ke 3 parosi H, 3 + 1 = 4: quartet.
• Area: CH₃ : CH₂ = 3 : 2.

Methoxymethane, CH₃–O–CH₃:
• Peaks: dono CH₃ groups aik environment mein, chhe protons equivalent: 1 peak.
• δ: CH₃–O, 3.0 – 4.5 ppm.
• Splitting: parosi O hai jis par H nahi, n = 0: singlet.
• Area: 6 H ki aik peak.

Farq: bromoethane mein do mukhtalif parosi proton sets hain jo aik doosre ko split karte hain; methoxymethane mein equivalent protons ka sirf aik set hai aur saath wale atom par protons nahi.

book_ref.quote: Predict the ¹H NMR spectrum of chloroethane (CH₃-CH₂-Cl).

blocks.prompt:
14 Describe how the structure of an unknown compound is deduced from its ¹H NMR spectrum. Explain the working of Example 30.2 (the ester). (4 marks)
(Na-maloom compound ki structure us ke ¹H NMR spectrum se kaise nikali jati hai, bayan karein. Example 30.2 (ester) ka tareeqa samjhayein.)
blocks.explanation:
Qadam (maloomaat ko puzzle ki tarah jorein):
1. Peaks ginein: proton environments (equivalent protons ke sets) ki tadaad, protons ki tadaad nahi.
2. Data table ke saath har chemical shift se functional groups pehchanein.
3. Peak areas se har environment ke H atoms maloom karein.
4. Splitting dekhein: n = sub-peaks – 1 parosi protons batata hai.
5. Maloomaat jorr kar structure banayein.

Example 30.2 (ester):

book_ref.quote: The structure of an unknown compound can also be deduced by analyzing its ¹H NMR spectrum

rows: electronegative O ke saath CH₂; n = 4 – 1 = 3 (CH₃–CH₂–O)

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Book ki table mein 3.9 ppm wali peak ko 'doublet' likha hai, magar CH₂ ke saath CH₃ ke teen protons hain aur spectrum quartet dikhata hai (Book correction). Isi tarah peaks ki tadaad environments batati hai, protons nahi.

blocks.prompt:
15 A compound C₂H₄O gives two ¹H NMR peaks: a doublet at 2.2 ppm and a quartet at 9.8 ppm, with relative areas 7.5 : 2.5. Deduce its structure, showing each step. (4 marks)
(Compound C₂H₄O do ¹H NMR peaks deta hai: 2.2 ppm par doublet aur 9.8 ppm par quartet, nisbati areas 7.5 : 2.5. Har qadam dikha kar is ki structure nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Peaks, areas, shifts aur splitting ko bari bari istemal karein, phir hisson ko jorein taake C₂H₄O se milein.

book_ref.quote: Count the number of peaks in the spectrum.

steps: Peaks = 2, yani do proton environments
Areas: 7.5/2.5 : 2.5/2.5 = 3 : 1; majmooa 4 = C₂H₄O ke 4 H, is liye 3 H aur 1 H
2.2 ppm (3 H): 2.0 – 2.6 ppm mein, C=O ke saath CH₃
9.8 ppm (1 H): 9.0 – 10.0 ppm mein, aldehyde proton –CHO
Splitting: CH₃ doublet, n = 2 – 1 = 1 (CHO hydrogen ke saath); CHO quartet, n = 4 – 1 = 3 (CH₃ ke saath)
Jorein: CH₃–CHO (C₂H₄O)

blocks.prompt:
16 A compound C₂H₄O₂ gives two singlets: 2.1 ppm and 11.4 ppm with relative areas 13.5 : 4.5. After a D₂O shake the 11.4 ppm peak disappears. Deduce the structure. (4 marks)
(Compound C₂H₄O₂ do singlets deta hai: 2.1 ppm aur 11.4 ppm, nisbati areas 13.5 : 4.5. D₂O shake ke baad 11.4 ppm wali peak ghayab ho jati hai. Structure nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Areas se har peak ke H nikalein, shifts se groups pehchanein, singlets (parosi nahi) aur D₂O natija (O–H) se inhein jorein.

book_ref.quote: Use peak area to find the actual number of hydrogen atoms for each peak

steps: Do peaks: do proton environments
Areas: 13.5/4.5 : 4.5/4.5 = 3 : 1; majmooa 4 = C₂H₄O₂ ke 4 H, is liye 3 H aur 1 H
2.1 ppm (3 H): 2.0 – 2.6 ppm mein, C=O ke saath CH₃; singlet, n = 0
11.4 ppm (1 H): 9.0 – 13.0 ppm mein, carboxylic acid; D₂O shake par ghayab, is liye O–H proton
Jorein: CH₃–COOH (C₂H₄O₂)

blocks.prompt:
17 Explain the basis of ¹³C NMR spectroscopy. Compare ¹H NMR and ¹³C NMR spectra. (4 marks)
(¹³C NMR spectroscopy ki bunyad samjhayein. ¹H NMR aur ¹³C NMR spectra ka muqabla karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Bunyad: ¹²C nucleus mein protons aur neutrons even (even mass number) hain, is liye magnetic property nahi aur woh NMR inactive hai. ¹³C nucleus mein neutrons odd hain, is liye magnetic spin hai aur carbon compounds ke ¹³C NMR spectra liye ja sakte hain.

¹H NMR ki tarah chemical shifts TMS (δ = 0.0 ppm) se nape jate hain, magar ¹³C range 0 – 220 ppm hai. Aam taur par solvent CDCl₃ hota hai; yeh 77 ppm ke qareeb chhota signal deta hai.

Muqabla:

book_ref.quote: On the basis of the magnetic properties of carbon-13 isotope

rows: Har peak = aik carbon environment; saada spectrum
Peak area protons ki tadaad batata hai
Peak area aam taur par carbons ki tadaad ke mutanasib nahi
Peaks split nahi hoti; seedhi lines

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Book mein CDCl₃ ka signal 80 ppm likha hai; durust value 77 ppm ke qareeb hai (Book correction).

blocks.prompt:
18 Explain the chemical environment of carbon atoms with examples. Give the chemical shift ranges of the main carbon environments from Table 30.3. (4 marks)
(Carbon atoms ke chemical environment ko misaalon se samjhayein. Table 30.3 se carbon ke bunyadi environments ki chemical shift ranges likhein.)
blocks.explanation:
Carbon atom ka environment us se seedhe jure atoms ki qisam se tay hota hai. Aik environment wale carbons chemically equivalent hain aur aik chemical shift dete hain; mukhtalif environments wale non-equivalent hain aur mukhtalif jagahon par aate hain.

Misaalein: ethane ke dono carbons ka environment aik hai. 2-methylpropane mein teen methyl carbons ka environment aik aur tertiary carbon ka mukhtalif (do environments).

Table 30.3:

book_ref.quote: The type of environment can be predicted by looking at atoms or bonds around carbon atoms

blocks.prompt:
19 How is a ¹³C NMR spectrum predicted? Predict and explain the ¹³C spectra of ethane, propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol, and interpret the spectrum of ethanol. (4 marks)
(¹³C NMR spectrum kaise predict hota hai? Ethane, propan-1-ol aur propan-2-ol ke ¹³C spectra predict kar ke samjhayein, aur ethanol ke spectrum ki tashreeh karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Har ¹³C peak aik mukhtalif carbon environment hai aur us ka chemical shift us environment ke baare mein batata hai:
Peaks ki tadaad = carbon ke mukhtalif environments ki tadaad

• Ethane, CH₃–CH₃: dono carbons aik environment mein: 1 peak.
• Propan-1-ol, CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–OH: teenon carbons mukhtalif: 3 peaks; sirf O se jura CH₂ C–O range 50 – 70 ppm mein.
• Propan-2-ol, (CH₃)₂CH–OH: dono CH₃ carbons equivalent, CH–OH carbon mukhtalif: 2 peaks; CH–O carbon 50 – 70 ppm par.

Ethanol, CH₃–CH₂–OH (Figure 30.7): do environments, do peaks. Table 30.3 se 18 ppm wali peak -CH₃ carbon ki aur 57 ppm ke qareeb wali oxygen se jure -CH₂- carbon ki hai.

Peaks split nahi hoti (seedhi lines) aur un ke areas aam taur par carbons ki tadaad ke mutanasib nahi hote.

book_ref.quote: Similarly, two peaks are observed in the ¹³C spectrum of ethanol

blocks.prompt:
20 Describe the steps used to determine a structure from a ¹³C NMR spectrum. A compound C₃H₈O shows 3 peaks, only one of which is in the range 50 – 70 ppm. Decide between propan-1-ol, propan-2-ol and methoxyethane (CH₃–O–CH₂–CH₃). (4 marks)
(¹³C NMR spectrum se structure nikalne ke qadam bayan karein. Compound C₃H₈O 3 peaks deta hai jin mein se sirf aik 50 – 70 ppm range mein hai. Propan-1-ol, propan-2-ol aur methoxyethane (CH₃–O–CH₂–CH₃) mein se faisla karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Qadam:
1. Peaks ginein: carbon ke mukhtalif environments ki tadaad. (Carbons se kam peaks ka matlab kuch carbons equivalent hain.)
2. Har peak ki jagah (δ) dekhein aur Table 30.3 se pehchanein (alkyl, O ke saath, alkene/aromatic, carbonyl ...).
3. Molecular formula se milne wali mumkina structures banayein, har aik ka spectrum sochein aur jo mile use rakhein.

C₃H₈O par istemal:
• Propan-2-ol, (CH₃)₂CH–OH: 2 environments, 2 peaks; tadaad se radd.
• Methoxyethane, CH₃–O–CH₂–CH₃: 3 environments, magar do carbons (CH₃–O aur O–CH₂) oxygen se jure hain, 50 – 70 ppm mein do peaks; jagah se radd.
• Propan-1-ol, CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–OH: 3 environments aur sirf aik carbon O se jura, is liye 50 – 70 ppm mein aik peak aur alkyl range mein do: milta hai.

Compound propan-1-ol hai. Book ki Figure 30.8 wali misaal dikhati hai ke sirf peaks ginna aik se zyada isomers se mil sakta hai; shifts bhi check karni chahiye.

blocks.text: Figure 30.8 mein book ne 2-methoxypropane chuna, magar shifts (69.0, 30.5, 19.0 ppm) mein sirf aik C–O carbon hai, jo 2-methylpropan-1-ol se milta hai (Book correction). Isi liye yahan count ke saath positions bhi dekhi gayi hain.
